exposure: obesity (body mass index of 30 kg/m or greater)
cohort: 692 patients who underwent benign vaginal hysterectomy between 2009 and 2013
finding: Vaginal hysterectomy can be performed safely and with favorable outcomes in women with a uterus greater than 280 g, prior cesarean delivery, no vaginal parity, and obesity, challenging perceived contraindications to this approach.
mod_finding: Prior cesarean delivery was significantly associated with an increased likelihood of uterine debulking.
